fields.reasoning: The finding is right: changeset.Kind is intention|record (internal/changeset/body.go:66-77), change new --kind takes intention|record, and change show --json already prints "kind" from c.Open.Kind, so reusing the name would collide, and a milestone request's change set must be kind record and milestone at once. The two are orthogonal (intention vs record is how a change set lands; feature/bug/milestone is what kind of request it came from), so they need two fields; overloading or replacing kind would break every existing log entry and the --kind flag. request_kind is the clearest name because the values are exactly the request kinds already fixed in internal/api/request.go (enum feature,bug,milestone, daemon.KindFeature/Bug/Milestone), it says where the value comes from, and it is the example name the plan reviewer and critic both proposed. Keeping the default feature for change sets no request opened matches @{01M6VYQWKXT7DC11ET2AAAER7G} and request.go's 'default feature', so the decision's rules are unchanged; only the field name is pinned.
fields.statement: The dispatch kind a change set records is a new field named request_kind (feature, bug or milestone), separate from the existing kind (intention or record), which keeps its meaning and values unchanged. The open entry carries request_kind next to the optional workflow; rhiza change show --json prints "request_kind" and "workflow" beside the existing "kind", and the text output labels it 'request kind'. A change set no request opened has request_kind feature, so a milestone request's change set reads kind record with request_kind milestone. @{01M6VYTAJBDW1YH8D7Y1XGCK76}'s statement and acceptance and @{01M6VYQWKXT7DC11ET2AAAER7G}'s wording 'records its kind' / 'kind bug' / 'kind feature' mean request_kind, and dispatch rules key on request_kind.
